tasks.short: Coordinate budgets, funding and investment choices across departments.

steps.what: Collect actuals, commitments, cash forecasts and departmental funding requests.
Reconcile departmental figures and assemble budget scenarios.
Read the financial pack and identify questions about variances and funding.

loop.input: Validated budget scenarios and source-linked department explanations.
loop.output: Financial review brief with variances, uncertainties and questions.
loop.check: Calculate figures deterministically; require source references and manager review of interpretations.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved claims revert to source tables.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but interpreting free-text explanations needs a bounded language step.

steps.what: Negotiate priorities, funding trade-offs and efficiency measures with department managers.
Approve funding within delegated limits or decide escalated requests.
Record approved budget changes and cost-centre allocations.
Chase agreed efficiency actions and report overdue commitments.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} data and feeds controlled scenarios in {BI}. A bounded drafting loop prepares source-linked review briefs; managers negotiate and approve funding through {WORKFLOW}. Approved decisions update the {ERP} and create tracked actions in {PROJECT}; payments remain separate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different account mappings, emailed assumptions and unclear approval limits made reliable consolidation expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing budget workflows and deterministic integrations handle most preparation. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort; a bounded drafting loop handles narrative explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling definitions, forecasting uncertain demand and settling competing departmental claims remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Judge which constraints matter, challenge optimistic assumptions and secure commitments from managers.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on small transfers between discretionary operating budgets.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling packs and more time testing funding choices. Weekly transfers become possible within an explicitly delegated limit; larger investment rights stay with authorised budget holders.

reach.task: Prepare a ranked portfolio of cross-department investment options.
reach.learn: Capital appraisal, liquidity constraints and how strategic priorities determine investment trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Deterministic reconciliation, scenario calculations and approval routing can automate much of the preparation.
Copilot in Power BI summarises reports and answers data questions; data-model quality constrains reliability.
Pigment reports major forecast and executive-reporting savings in vendor cases; these do not establish savings here.

assumptions: Time shares are illustrative estimates for a recurring departmental budget cycle.
Financial decisions remain human; most change concerns preparation, recording and follow-up.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot with reusable connectors, not replacement of the finance architecture.
Access estimates include confidentiality review and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Available interfaces, account mappings and quality of commitment data.
Who can approve budget transfers and investment requests.
Whether existing planning workflows can record approvals and write budgets.
Whether any employee-level data is needed.
research_questions: Which reconciliation differences require judgement rather than mapping rules?
Does the existing budget module support the required scenario and approval process?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation exceptions and stale source data.
Review narrative explanations against cited figures.
Maintain account mappings, scenario assumptions and approval limits.
Monitor failed writes and duplicate decision records.

tasks.short: Coordinate cross-department initiatives, including sales promotions, from proposal through launch and review.

steps.what: Define the initiative's objective, scope and success measures.
Gather departmental capacity, dependencies and objections from messages.

loop.input: Department responses linked to one initiative.
loop.output: Readiness brief listing constraints, dependencies, proposed owners and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Link every item to its message; distinguish proposals from accepted commitments.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unclear commitments remain unresolved for discussion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text responses express qualifications and objections that fixed fields cannot reliably capture.

steps.what: Resolve dependencies and agree departmental commitments.
Translate agreed commitments into a schedule with owners and dependencies.
Approve promotional launch after reviewing content, stock, service capacity and spend.
Chase milestone updates and escalate missed dependencies.
Review commercial results and agree changes for the next initiative.

tasks.design: Configure initiative templates, dependency checks and reminders in {PROJECT}, with structured readiness responses in {WORKFLOW}. A bounded loop turns remaining {EMAIL} and {CHAT} responses into a source-linked brief, while {BI} supplies results for review. Managers settle commitments and the campaign owner approves each external launch in {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Commitments were scattered across messages, and project records did not reliably reflect what departments had agreed.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project workflows can handle schedules and reminders. Small integrations and bounded extraction can connect the remaining narrative responses.
tasks.still_hard: Capacity conflicts, disputed ownership and commercial timing require negotiation. A complete checklist cannot establish that a launch is wise.
tasks.human_edge: Build commitment between managers and recognise when an apparently ready initiative will strain customer service or operations.

ambition.what: A weekly cross-department launch-readiness clinic for initiative owners.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing updates and more time resolving launch constraints. They can recommend resequencing initiatives using shared capacity evidence; launch and spending rights remain explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Recommend which competing initiatives should receive scarce cross-department capacity.
reach.learn: Portfolio prioritisation, contribution margins and organisation-wide capacity trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Project templates, dependency rules and scheduled reminders can handle routine coordination.
The cross-government trial reported drafting savings but variable benefits; it does not establish initiative-coordination savings.
Source-linked extraction can prepare discussions without treating an inferred commitment as an accepted one.

assumptions: The steps illustrate a sales promotion; other initiatives use the same coordination pattern.
Time shares preserve the substantial human work in planning and agreement.
Build ranges cover one initiative template and a small set of connected systems.
Access work includes checking national consultation requirements if individual work tracking changes.
unknowns: Which role owns launch approval and which readiness checks are mandatory.
Whether departments maintain current capacity and milestone records.
Whether reminders would introduce new employee monitoring.
research_questions: Which readiness questions can move from messages into existing structured forms?
Which dependency failures recur often enough for deterministic escalation?
new_work: Check extracted constraints and proposed commitments.
Maintain initiative templates and escalation thresholds.
Resolve contradictory updates and stale milestones.
Review whether reminders create noise or encourage superficial status reporting.

tasks.short: Select staff, agree training and conduct performance evaluations with personnel support.

steps.what: For hiring, assemble applications, interview criteria and approved role requirements.
Interview candidates and discuss evidence against the role criteria.
Select a candidate and record the evidence and proposed terms.
Prepare and issue the offer using approved terms.
For training, compare role requirements with course and certification records.
Discuss development needs and agree learning priorities with the employee.
Enrol the employee in agreed courses and set completion reminders.
For evaluation, assemble agreed goals, employee submissions and previous review records.
Discuss performance evidence, context and development with the employee.
Write and approve the assessment, recording employee comments and agreed actions.

tasks.design: Configure packs and approval routes in the {ATS}, role-based training checks in the {LMS}, and review preparation in {TALENT}. Approved fields populate offer templates in {DOCS} for authorised release through {ESIGN}, while agreed learning plans create {LMS} enrolments. Interviews, development conversations, candidate selection and performance assessments remain human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate personnel systems and inconsistent templates left managers and personnel staff assembling records manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing personnel modules often cover these workflows. Configuration and small deterministic connectors can remove preparation work without introducing model-based evaluation.
tasks.still_hard: Fair selection, candid feedback and understanding personal context remain human work. GDPR, access controls and national employment and consultation rules constrain how records are used.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise potential, hear an employee's explanation and take responsibility for decisions affecting their working life.

ambition.what: Offer a structured development conversation to shift employees outside the annual review window.

tasks.altitude: The manager gains time for interviews and development conversations, with less personnel paperwork. Hiring, training-spend and assessment rights do not change automatically.

reach.task: Identify organisation-wide capability gaps for workforce planning.
reach.learn: Aggregate workforce planning, succession risks and privacy-preserving use of personnel information.

evidence.claim: Pack assembly, approved-field offer generation and course enrolment are suitable for existing software configuration.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
AI used for recruitment decisions or staff performance evaluation can fall within Annex III high-risk categories.

assumptions: These are three recurring branches: hiring, learning and evaluation, not one sequence for every employee.
Shares represent an illustrative mix of those branches across the manager's personnel work.
Training checks use explicit role requirements and completion records, not inferred personal traits.
No model ranks candidates, scores employees or recommends employment consequences.
Build ranges include access design, employee consultation and works-council involvement where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which personnel modules and template features are enabled.
The manager's actual hiring and assessment authority.
Applicable national rules, collective agreements and consultation arrangements.
Lawful bases, retention periods and access permissions for each personnel record.
How much work falls into hiring, learning and evaluation locally.
research_questions: Which preparation steps can existing personnel modules already perform?
Which proposed changes alter monitoring or personnel decision processes and therefore require consultation?
Can capability reporting use aggregated records without exposing individual assessments?
new_work: Maintain role requirements, approved templates and enrolment rules.
Resolve incomplete or conflicting personnel records.
Audit access permissions and retention settings.
Handle employee corrections and challenges to recorded evidence.

tasks.short: Develop departmental policies, goals and procedures with leaders and staff, then coordinate implementation.

steps.what: Collect existing policies, operational evidence and staff proposals.

loop.input: An approved collection of current policies, operational evidence and staff proposals.
loop.output: Source-linked evidence brief listing issues, existing requirements and conflicting proposals.
loop.check: Require a source location for each claim; verify document versions and review contradictions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unsupported claims are omitted and gaps listed.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text proposals and policy documents express overlapping or conflicting requirements.

steps.what: Agree goals, policy choices and practical constraints with leaders and staff.
Draft the policy, procedures, goal definitions and implementation responsibilities.

loop.input: Agreed direction, proposed goals, controlled template and source-linked evidence brief.
loop.output: Policy draft and implementation plan with unresolved choices explicitly marked.
loop.check: Compare every obligation, target and named responsibility with agreed inputs; verify cited sources.
loop.stop: One draft and two revision passes; unresolved policy choices return to the policy owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but expressing agreed choices as clear procedures requires language drafting.

steps.what: Review legal, personnel, financial and operational implications.
Approve the policy and goals after resolving material objections.
Publish the approved version and notify affected staff.
Track implementation actions and assemble evidence of adoption.

tasks.design: Use controlled templates and versioned sources in {DOCS}, with bounded loops preparing evidence briefs and policy drafts. A configured {WORKFLOW} routes specialist reviews and records approval of an exact version before publication in {DOCS}. The approved implementation plan creates actions in {PROJECT} and feeds an adoption view in {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy evidence and comments were dispersed across documents and meetings, while drafting required substantial manual synthesis.
tasks.enabler_now: Version control and approval workflows already handle publication. Bounded extraction and drafting can reduce synthesis work when sources and agreed decisions are explicit.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing legitimate goals, resolving conflicting interests and interpreting applicable law require responsible people. Completion records do not prove that a policy works in practice.
tasks.human_edge: Decide what the organisation should require and secure acceptance from the people who must implement it.

ambition.what: Quarterly decisions on whether departmental procedures should be revised using implementation evidence.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rewriting documents and more time testing whether procedures achieve their goals. They can sponsor evidence-based revisions; formal policy approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Recommend which departmental policy experiments should become organisation-wide standards.
reach.learn: Governance mandates, consultation duties and evaluation of policy outcomes across departments.

evidence.claim: Board Intelligence Report Writer drafts structured papers from management documents, supporting the feasibility of bounded document preparation.
The documented flawed government report illustrates why generated references must be checked before approval.
Version-controlled publication and approval routing can be configured without model judgement.

assumptions: The policy owner supplies authoritative sources and agreed choices; the model does not invent requirements.
Time shares are illustrative for a substantive departmental policy change.
Publication is limited to the exact approved version and audience.
Build ranges cover one policy family and include access review and consultation planning.
Employee consultation or works-council involvement follows applicable national rules; substantive negotiations may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Who has authority to approve each policy type.
Which national consultation requirements and collective agreements apply.
Whether the document store supports version-specific approval and publication.
Which evidence can measure adoption without creating unnecessary employee monitoring.
Whether policy changes require system changes beyond document publication.
research_questions: Which sources are authoritative when existing policies conflict?
Can the approval workflow prevent publication of a modified, unapproved version?
Which outcome measures distinguish practical improvement from administrative completion?
new_work: Verify source references and remove unsupported obligations.
Maintain templates, source ownership and review dates.
Resolve specialist objections and consultation outcomes.
Handle failed publication or distribution rules.
Assess whether implementation evidence justifies revising the policy.

role.altitude: The operations manager spends more of the week resolving cross-department trade-offs, developing people and testing whether agreed changes work. Better preparation supports more frequent decisions within delegated authority; it does not itself expand approval rights.
reach: Prepare cross-department investment and initiative priorities for the chief executive.
Translate aggregate capability gaps into workforce-planning options.
Recommend which departmental procedures merit organisation-wide adoption.
skills_to_grow: Financial scenario analysis and investment appraisal.
Evidence-based interviewing, feedback and development planning.
Source verification and critical review of generated drafts.
Data definitions, access governance and exception handling.
Policy evaluation and consultation under applicable national rules.
role.ambitious_version: Run a regular operating review that connects funding choices, initiative capacity, workforce development and policy outcomes, bringing the chief executive concrete options with clear trade-offs.
